children: Waaree Energies will supply solar modules to a leading domestic solar developer across FY27 and FY28, with the order value undisclosed

Waaree Energies shares gained nearly 2 per cent in early trade on Tuesday after the renewable energy company announced a 2 GW solar module supply order from a leading domestic solar developer, adding to its sizeable module pipeline amid continued expansion in India’s solar capacity. The order, secured on 21 September and to be executed across FY27 and FY28, comes as the company’s module order book stands at about 25.2 GW. The customer’s identity and financial value of the contract were not disclosed.

The company’s shares climbed 1.90 per cent to an intraday high of Rs 2,548.45 on the National Stock Exchange, compared with the previous close of Rs 2,501. The stock had opened at Rs 2,540 and touched an intraday low of Rs 2,520.60 during Tuesday’s session.

Waaree Energies said the contract involves a one time supply of 2 GW of solar modules to a domestic entity that it described as a renowned customer and leading solar developer. The company has not disclosed the commercial consideration for the order.
It also said the transaction does not qualify as a related party transaction and that neither the promoter nor the promoter group has any interest in the entity awarding the contract.

The latest contract adds to Waaree Energies module supply pipeline as demand for solar generation capacity and related infrastructure expands in India. The company had an order book of around Rs 61,500 crore as of 28 July, 2026, its highest reported level, with module orders accounting for about 90 per cent of the total.

Its module order book stood at around 25.2 GW, according to its investor presentation. In the first quarter of FY27, Waaree Energies reported a 14 per cent year over year increase in net profit to Rs 850 crore, while revenue from operations rose 79 per cent to Rs 7,932 crore, according to company related disclosures, as per news reports.
